name: saleor
purpose: Saleor is an open-source (BSD-3), headless, GraphQL-only commerce backend: merchants and their developers run it to sell products across channels, currencies and warehouses, and plug in payments, taxes, shipping and custom logic as separate apps over webhooks.
stage: Live, mature product: version 3.24.0-a.0 on main (3.x is the production line), deployed as many identical pods on Kubernetes, with Saleor Cloud as the company's hosted offering.

audiences.name: Merchants (store owners)
audiences.description: Businesses that sell through Saleor; they configure channels, catalog, prices, discounts and payment strategy, usually through the separate Dashboard.

audiences.name: Merchant staff
audiences.description: Staff users with permission groups who manage orders, refunds, gift cards and customers.

audiences.name: Shoppers
audiences.description: End customers, signed-in or guest, who browse via a storefront, check out and pay.

audiences.name: Storefront and integration developers
audiences.description: Developers who build storefronts and apps against the GraphQL API; Saleor targets teams that deploy daily and need uptime.

audiences.name: App and payment-provider builders
audiences.description: Third parties whose apps install from a manifest, get permissions and a token, and answer payment, tax and shipping webhooks.

audiences.name: Saleor Cloud customers
audiences.description: Teams who use Saleor Commerce's hosted Saleor Cloud instead of self-hosting.

value.name: One GraphQL API for all of commerce
value.description: Catalog, checkout, orders, payments, discounts and taxes behind a single /graphql/ endpoint; no lock-in to a frontend stack.

value.name: Multi-channel, multi-currency selling
value.description: Each Channel has its own currency, country, stock allocation, payment and order rules, and per-channel prices.

value.name: Payment orchestration without core changes
value.description: Any PSP can be plugged in as an app answering TRANSACTION_* webhooks; Saleor keeps the ledger of authorized, charged, refunded amounts.

value.name: Promotions, vouchers and gift cards
value.description: Promotion rules, voucher codes and bearer gift cards reduce what the shopper pays.

value.name: Extend by apps, not plugins
value.description: Apps are deployed independently and receive events over HTTP, AWS SQS or Google Pub/Sub, so custom logic does not touch the core.

value.name: Free and open source
value.description: Everything in the repository is free to use under the license; no hidden charges.

money_flows.name: Shopper pays merchant through a payment app (transaction flow)
money_flows.description: The storefront calls transactionInitialize/transactionProcess; Saleor forwards TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION / TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION sync webhooks to the payment app, which talks to the PSP. Results are stored as TransactionItem amounts (authorized, charged, refunded, canceled). Money moves between shopper, PSP and merchant; Saleor records it but does not hold funds.

money_flows.name: Legacy payment flow (Payment model and gateway plugins)
money_flows.description: Older Payment objects with ChargeStatus and the built-in Stripe gateway plugin, which handles Stripe payment intents and verifies the stripe-signature header. Channel default is still PAYMENT_FLOW.

money_flows.name: Merchant refunds shopper
money_flows.description: Staff grant refunds (OrderGrantedRefund) and request refund/charge/cancel actions; Saleor sends TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED / CHARGE / CANCELATION to the app that owns the transaction.

money_flows.name: Funds released on abandoned checkouts
money_flows.description: A task every 10 minutes cancels or refunds payments on checkouts that were paid but never completed, when the channel opts in (release_funds_for_expired_checkouts, default off; TTL 6 hours).

money_flows.name: Gift cards as stored value
money_flows.description: Gift cards are bearer instruments with a balance; they can be bought as order lines, are fulfilled and sent to the buyer, and spent at checkout. Balance changes must be atomic.

money_flows.name: Discounts reduce the price
money_flows.description: Promotions (catalogue and order rules) and vouchers lower line and order prices; the discounted price is recalculated by scheduled tasks.

money_flows.name: Taxes calculated by flat rates or a tax app
money_flows.description: Per channel and country, tax is either flat rates kept in Saleor or computed by a tax app over CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES / ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES; a deprecated built-in Avalara plugin remains.

money_flows.name: How Saleor Commerce (the company) earns money
money_flows.description: The README points to Saleor Cloud sign-up and a sales contact, but no pricing, plans or billing code are in this repository.

journeys.name: Shopper buys with a payment app
journeys.outcome: A placed, paid order and reserved stock

steps.name: Browse catalog in a channel
steps.description: Storefront queries products with per-channel prices and availability through /graphql/.

steps.name: Create checkout and add lines
steps.description: checkoutCreate / checkoutLinesAdd; stock can be reserved per checkout line.

steps.name: Pick delivery and get taxes
steps.description: Shipping methods and taxes may come from apps through sync webhooks.

steps.name: Apply vouchers, promotions, gift cards
steps.description: Discounts and gift cards change the total.

steps.name: Pay through a payment app
steps.description: transactionInitialize then transactionProcess call the payment app; the TransactionItem records authorized or charged amounts.

steps.name: Complete checkout
steps.description: checkoutComplete creates the order once transactions cover the total (or unpaid orders are allowed); a lock prevents double completion. It can also run automatically for fully paid checkouts.

steps.name: Apps are notified
steps.description: ORDER_CREATED and similar async events go to subscribed apps, deferred and built from the replica.

journeys.name: Merchant fulfils, refunds or expires an order
journeys.outcome: Order moves to fulfilled, returned, refunded, canceled or expired

steps.name: Confirm the order
steps.description: Channels confirm new orders automatically by default; otherwise staff confirm.

steps.name: Fulfil from warehouses
steps.description: Stock is allocated per warehouse; gift card lines are fulfilled and sent automatically.

steps.name: Charge or refund
steps.description: Staff grant refunds and request charge/refund/cancel on transactions; the payment app executes them.

steps.name: Expire unpaid orders
steps.description: A beat task expires unpaid orders after the channel's expire_orders_after and deletes them later.

journeys.name: Developer installs an app (e.g. a payment or tax app)
journeys.outcome: An app with permissions and webhooks that Saleor calls

steps.name: Install from a manifest
steps.description: install_app reads the manifest, creates the App with granted permissions, its webhooks and dashboard extensions.

steps.name: Receive events
steps.description: Webhooks go out over HTTP, AWS SQS or Google Pub/Sub; payloads can be deferred or immediate.

steps.name: Verify signatures
steps.description: Saleor publishes its public keys at /.well-known/jwks.json so receivers can verify signed payloads.

steps.name: Answer sync webhooks
steps.description: Payment, tax and shipping apps must answer within the sync timeout.

systems.name: saleor (package.json)
systems.description: Not an app: package.json only holds release-it tooling for versioning (3.24.0-a.0).

systems.name: Saleor API (Django + GraphQL)
systems.description: Python 3.12 Django app served by uvicorn (saleor.asgi:application), exposing /graphql/, plugin webhooks, thumbnails and JWKS; Celery workers run background tasks.

systems.name: stripe
systems.description: Stripe SDK used by the built-in legacy Stripe gateway plugin (payment intents, signed webhooks).

systems.name: authlib
systems.description: OAuth/OIDC library, used by the OpenID Connect plugin for staff/customer login.

systems.name: pyjwt
systems.description: JWT tokens for API auth and signing; public keys at /.well-known/jwks.json.

systems.name: psycopg
systems.description: Postgres driver; Postgres (with read replicas) is the shared system of record.

systems.name: redis
systems.description: Redis/Valkey client: cache, Celery broker, circuit-breaker storage.

systems.name: celery
systems.description: Celery workers and beat schedule (expiry, cleanups, price recalculation, auto-completion).

systems.name: boto3
systems.description: AWS SDK: S3 media storage and SQS webhook transport.

systems.name: google-cloud-storage
systems.description: Google Cloud Storage for media files.

systems.name: sentry-sdk
systems.description: Error reporting to Sentry when configured.

systems.name: Postgres (primary + read replicas)
systems.description: Shared database for every pod; the scaling bottleneck.

systems.name: Payment apps (external)
systems.description: Any PSP integration as a Saleor app answering TRANSACTION_* and PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION webhooks.

systems.name: Tax apps and Avalara
systems.description: Tax apps over CHECKOUT/ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES; deprecated built-in Avalara plugin.

systems.name: Google Cloud Pub/Sub and AWS SQS
OpenTelemetry
systems.description: Built-in tracing and metrics instrumentation (psycopg, celery, redis, requests, botocore).

systems.name: Saleor usage telemetry
systems.description: Daily usage report to usage-telemetry.saleor.io, on by default.

systems.name: Dashboard and storefront (other repositories)
systems.description: Admin UI and example Next.js storefront live in separate repositories.

risks.name: Checkout depends on synchronous calls to apps
risks.description: Payment sessions, taxes and shipping-method lists are sync webhooks with a 2s connect + 18s read timeout. A slow or down app stalls or breaks checkout; the circuit breaker exists but is off by default and must be configured per event.
risks.signal: p95 latency and error rate of sync webhooks by event type and app; breaker trips

risks.name: Two payment models coexist
risks.description: complete_checkout picks the transaction flow or the legacy payment flow from authorize status, active payment, allowUnpaidOrders and the channel's mark-as-paid strategy. Misconfigured channels can create unpaid orders or block completion.
risks.signal: orders created with charge status below total; checkoutComplete errors by channel

risks.name: Transaction token is a bearer capability
risks.description: The transaction id/token is accepted by unauthenticated transactionInitialize/transactionProcess, so exposing it leaks a capability; ADR-0010 builds a projection to avoid that.
risks.signal: any new field or log that returns TransactionItem.token to public callers

risks.name: Async webhooks carry current, not historical, state
risks.description: Deferred payloads are built in a background task from the read replica; two quick mutations give identical deliveries and a deleted object gives none. Integrations that replay changes in order can go wrong.
risks.signal: FAILED deliveries for deleted objects; app complaints about missing intermediate states

risks.name: Shared database under concurrent pods
risks.description: Every request can run on any pod against one Postgres; check-then-act code, long select_for_update or N+1 queries are the main scaling and correctness risk (gift card balance, stock allocation, checkout completion lock).
risks.signal: lock waits, deadlocks, negative or drifted quantity_allocated, double-charged gift cards

risks.name: Background tasks and multi-site deployments
risks.description: One process may serve several sites, and Site.objects.get_current() falls back to the request host. Beat tasks such as expire_orders_task have no request, so in a multi-site deployment they may apply one site's settings to all.
risks.signal: orders expiring or not expiring per site differently from their site settings

risks.name: Storefront traffic blocking is not a security control
risks.description: When enabled it rejects after parsing, may lag because of cache and replica, and also blocks login and introspection; deployers must still run a WAF.
risks.signal: 401 rate and CPU on HTTP workers while blocking is on

risks.name: Usage telemetry is on by default
risks.description: SEND_USAGE_TELEMETRY defaults to True and posts usage data to usage-telemetry.saleor.io; self-hosters with data-residency rules may not expect this.

improvements.description: Enable BREAKER_BOARD for payment, tax and shipping events (dry-run first) so one failing app does not take checkout down.

improvements.name: Make beat tasks iterate sites explicitly
improvements.description: Resolve each site in background tasks instead of get_current() without a request.
